headline: Geopolitical Friction Fuels Commodities; Software Bleeds Into the Close
body_html:
Friday's session closed with a split personality: raw-materials and energy names surged while software and consumer shares surrendered ground, leaving the broader tape marginally negative at the bell. Of 549 names tracked, 259 advanced against 287 decliners — a subtle but meaningful tilt toward defensiveness even as risk appetite flared in pockets. The dominant theme was unmistakable: mounting tension around the Strait of Hormuz, tanker attacks in the region, and reports of slowing traffic through one of the world's most critical oil chokepoints combined to push energy prices sharply higher, dragging the Energy sector up 1.35% and lifting Materials 1.24%.

Semiconductors proved a notable bright spot, gaining 1.13% on the session. Flash-memory dynamics supplied fresh catalysts, with Sandisk surging 7.39% and MaxLinear — the day's standout — vaulting 10.68% on bullish signals emanating from the memory supply chain. AMD added 6.50%, reinforcing the chip-complex's resilience. On the other side of the ledger, Software shed 1.37%, the worst sectoral reading of the day, with enterprise and cybersecurity names leading that retreat.

The commodity-driven outperformance is worth watching heading into next week. When energy and materials lead simultaneously on geopolitical supply fears rather than demand optimism, the signal is cautionary — markets are pricing risk premiums, not growth. That distinction matters.

briefs.headline: MaxLinear Caps a Remarkable Week With Double-Digit Surge
briefs.body: MaxLinear led the entire universe on Friday, climbing 10.68% as favorable developments in the flash-memory supply chain reverberated across related chipmakers. The move capped a strong stretch for the semiconductor complex and underscored how quickly sentiment can reprice around supply-side inflection points in the memory ecosystem.

briefs.headline: Hormuz Tensions Drive Energy Sector to Session's Top Spot
briefs.body: Reports of tanker attacks, dueling US-Iran claims over control of the Strait of Hormuz, and visibly slower traffic through the waterway sent oil prices climbing and pushed the Energy sector up 1.35% on the day. The developments added a geopolitical risk premium that rippled from crude markets into commodity-linked equities broadly.

briefs.headline: Gulf Oil Spill Off Oman Compounds Regional Shipping Anxiety
briefs.body: Separately from the Hormuz standoff, two oil slicks appeared in the Gulf following a reported large-scale spill off Oman's coast, adding another layer of concern for shipping routes and regional supply logistics. Energy investors tracked both stories simultaneously as the sector closed atop the day's sector leaderboard.

briefs.headline: Software Sector Posts Sharpest Decline of Any Group Friday
briefs.body: Software gave back 1.37%, the weakest reading across all tracked sectors. N-able fell 6.11% and ZoomInfo dropped 6.03%, while Qualys shed 5.02% — a broad-based retreat that suggested profit-taking and positioning adjustments ahead of the weekend rather than any single catalyst driving the group lower.

briefs.headline: Copart Charges Higher After Spin-Off Signals Attract Buyers
briefs.body: Auto-auction platform Copart jumped 7.55%, one of the sharpest non-semiconductor gains of the session. The move appeared tied to renewed investor enthusiasm around recent corporate spin-off activity, with buyers stepping in to build exposure to what they view as a favorable long-term structural story in the vehicle-remarketing space.

briefs.headline: Homebuilder Stocks Slip as Housing Investor Sentiment Sours
briefs.body: The Homebuilders sector declined 0.58% Friday as commentary from property investors described current conditions as the most difficult in at least three years. The backdrop of elevated rates and strained affordability continued to weigh on sentiment in the segment even as broader equity markets attempted to stabilize around a recent record close.
